terms.gloss: remind (someone of something; to do something)
terms.grammar: verb, second conjugation; the person in the accusative, the thing in the genitive or with dē, an action with ut or nē
evidence: Cic. Top. 5: admonitus hujus aeris aliēnī (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: To put someone in mind of a thing, kindly (Lewis & Short); also to advise and to warn. The simple moneō serves too, especially in thanks: bene monēs.

evidence: Cic. Fam. 13.72.1: etiam atque etiam esse commonefaciendum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Stronger than admonēre: to remind again and again (Lewis & Short: “most freq. in Cic.”). So too commoneō.

phrases.latin: sōl mē invītābat, famēs admonēbat, nūbēs minābantur
phrases.english: the sun invited me out, hunger reminded me, the clouds threatened

phrases.latin: Bene monēs, paene istud oblītus eram.
phrases.english: Thanks for reminding me, I had nearly forgotten.

sources: Lewis & Short: admoneo · Lewis & Short: commonefacio · Lewis & Short: commoneo
Quotations from the Latinitas loci collections (loci-seneca-epistulae, loci-corderius), checked against the editions named there.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, with its references, in the house spelling (macrons, consonantal j); they have not been checked against a modern edition.
